v.q: What does separating deploy from release allow?
o: Deploying code with a feature still off
Skipping the pipeline for small changes
v.w: The code goes live with the flag off. The release, switching it on, is a separate and reversible step.

v.q: Which statement about releasing is true?
o: It exposes a feature to users
v.w: Releasing is a business decision about who sees a feature. Deploying is the technical step of installing a version.

v.q: What is the main limit of a rolling update?
o: Two versions serve traffic at the same time
v.w: During the update old and new versions run together, so their APIs and the database schema must be compatible.

v.q: Which setting keeps full capacity during a Kubernetes rolling update?
v.w: A surge pod starts first and no pod may go missing, so the ready count never drops below the desired one.

v.q: What happens when a new pod never passes its readiness probe?
o: It gets no traffic and the rollout stalls
The old pods are all removed
v.w: The controller keeps the old pods serving, so users are not affected, and the rollout fails after its deadline.

v.q: Why add a short preStop sleep?
o: The load balancer stops sending traffic first
v.w: Endpoint updates take a moment, so the pod waits a few seconds before it starts to stop, and no request meets a closed server.

v.q: What is the biggest benefit of blue-green deployment?
o: It runs both versions for users
v.w: The old environment is untouched, so switching the router back restores the previous version at once.

v.q: Which is a cost of blue-green deployment?
o: Two full environments during the release
Users see a mix of versions
No way to test before the switch
v.w: Both environments run at the same time. They also usually share one database, which must suit both versions.

v.q: What is the main benefit of a canary release?
o: A small blast radius with real traffic
v.w: Only a few users meet a bad release, and the data comes from real production traffic.

v.q: Against what should a canary be compared?
o: The stable version at the same time
The same metric from last year
v.w: Both versions face the same traffic and conditions, so a difference points at the new version.

v.q: What is the main risk of shadow traffic?
o: Side effects such as charges or emails
v.w: The shadow gets real requests, so it must be read-only or stubbed, or it may charge cards or send messages.

v.q: Which problem comes with feature flags?
v.w: Each flag adds paths to test. Give every flag an owner and a removal date.

v.q: Which step comes last in expand and contract?
v.w: The old structure is removed in a later release, when no old version can return.

v.q: Why is a column rename dangerous in a rolling update?
o: The old version breaks at once
v.w: The old pods are still running against the same database, so removing the name they use breaks them.

v.q: When is recreate a reasonable choice?
v.w: It causes a gap, so use it for batch jobs, test environments or incompatible changes in a maintenance window.

v.w: Rollbacks that were never run often break, especially after a database change.
